name: Atlantis
lede: Atlantis is a dark, slightly greenish navy from Maerz and Paul's 1930 color dictionary; why it carries the lost island's name is undocumented.

sections.title: A dictionary name
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's *Dictionary of Color* (1930) lists Atlantis at plate 39, position L 8, and the NBS Circular 553 of 1955 cites it [1]. The earliest recorded use the library finds is 1928, and the nearest ISCC-NBS category is deep greenish blue, about 6.6 units away [1]. Who chose the name, and why, is undocumented; the color books we hold mention the word only in a bibliography entry, not as a color [2]. Its twin is [[glacier]], 2.6 units away, followed by [[freedom]] and [[dark-grey-blue]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Atlantis appears in 238 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 1.0%, as photographed [4]. It peaks in paintings of the 1900s, in 36 of 1,674 (2.2%), 3.3 times the rate expected from the same museums [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 48% of the 122 paintings where it counts, judged by lightness rank [4]. The earliest painting is from 1301, though the archive is thin in early centuries [4]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test.
